episodes.title: 12 Years No Contact with a Narcissistic Mother | Healing, Triangulation & Life After Abuse
episodes.description: What happens after you walk away from a narcissistic mother? What does life look like 12 years later, when you're no longer simply surviving but finally learning how to live? In this special episode of Beyond Mommy Dearest, host Noelani Pearl Hernandez welcomes back Kylie B., known as The Narcissist's Daughter, to celebrate her 12th Rebirthday—12 years since she reclaimed her independence. And this time, we're not focusing only on what happened to us. We're celebrating everything that came afterward. The friendships restored. The families we chose. The love we learned to accept. The milestones we once never imagined we'd reach. Kylie shares one of the most heartbreaking—and ultimately beautiful—stories from her healing journey. When she was a teenager, she believed her childhood best friend had abandoned her. Her mother repeatedly reinforced that belief, convincing Kylie that her friend had moved on without her. More than 15 years later, the two finally discovered the truth. Her best friend had been knocking on her door every single day. Her mother had been turning her away. Two young girls spent years believing they'd rejected each other, when the reality was that someone had deliberately interfered with their friendship. Today, they're reunited, celebrating their friendship, laughing like the eight-year-olds they once were, and reclaiming the joy that was stolen from them. But that's only part of this conversation. Kylie and Noelani explore what happens when survivors begin building genuinely healthy relationships—and discover that accepting love, praise, safety, and happiness can sometimes feel just as unfamiliar as navigating trauma. They discuss chosen mothers, supportive friendships, emotional exhaustion, recognizing unhealthy relationship patterns, learning to celebrate personal accomplishments, and why healing doesn't mean you'll never experience another difficult moment. They also get candid about protecting their children, navigating online toxicity, the influence of social media, and the importance of finding people who genuinely want to see you succeed. And, of course, there's plenty of laughter, a few colorful words, and some wonderfully inappropriate humor along the way. In this episode, we explore: What 12 years of no contact can look like. How narcissistic mothers can sabotage their daughters' friendships through triangulation. Reconnecting with people you believed had abandoned you. Why receiving healthy love can feel uncomfortable after childhood emotional abuse. Finding chosen mothers, sisters, and supportive communities. Recognizing when friendships no longer align with your growth. Learning to celebrate yourself without guilt or shame. The difference between relationships that replenish your energy and those that drain it. Why feeling safe can reveal entirely new layers of healing. Reclaiming childhood joy, playfulness, and the freedom to be yourself. One of the most important reminders from this conversation: You can have a difficult year and still have a beautiful life. You can experience grief and gratitude simultaneously. You can make mistakes, outgrow relationships, and discover new parts of yourself. And you can build a life filled with people whose love doesn't come with conditions. If you're newly no contact, considering estrangement, or wondering whether life ever gets better after narcissistic parental abuse, this episode offers something incredibly important: A glimpse of what life can look like on the other side. Happy 12th Rebirthday, Kylie. Here's to everything you've reclaimed—and everything still waiting for you. episodes.title: When Your Mother Controls Your Reality: Narcissistic Abuse, Family Cults & Healing
episodes.description: In this deeply personal episode of Beyond Mommy Dearest, host Noelani Pearl Hernandez sits down with Orenda Fink, author of The Witch's Daughter, former musician, writer, Jungian coach, and narcissistic abuse recovery coach, for a powerful conversation about growing up with a mother whose stories, beliefs, and emotional instability shaped the family's entire reality. Orenda shares her extraordinary childhood, growing up with a mother who claimed magical abilities, practiced witchcraft, and created an environment filled with fear, confusion, and chaos. As a child, Orenda struggled to distinguish reality from the stories her mother told. As an adult, she began uncovering how deeply those experiences shaped her identity, relationships, and understanding of love. Noelani and Orenda explore the psychological impact of narcissistic family systems, the connections between dysfunctional families and cult-like dynamics, and why survivors often find themselves unconsciously recreating the chaos they worked so hard to escape. They also discuss the heartbreaking reality of going no contact with parents who are still alive, the complicated grief that follows, and why choosing safety doesn't mean you've stopped loving someone. Through Orenda's experience with Jungian psychology, shadow work, and narcissistic abuse recovery, the conversation examines how survivors can begin recognizing their triggers, challenging the beliefs planted during childhood, and rediscovering who they are outside their family's expectations. In this episode, we explore: Growing up with a narcissistic mother: How fabricated stories, magical thinking, and emotional instability can shape a child's understanding of reality. The cult of the family: Why narcissistic family systems can resemble high-control groups, including their demands for loyalty, obedience, and emotional compliance. Highly sensitive children and hypervigilance: How growing up in unpredictable environments can influence the way children process danger, relationships, and emotions. Why chaos can feel familiar: How childhood survival strategies may carry into romantic relationships, friendships, and professional environments. Jungian psychology and shadow work: Understanding triggers, unconscious patterns, and the parts of ourselves we learned to reject to survive. The grief of no contact: Why estrangement can be devastating even when it is necessary for emotional or physical safety. Learning to prioritize yourself: Why survivors who were taught to be endlessly selfless may struggle with boundaries and healthy self-interest. Gray rocking and yellow rocking: Practical communication strategies for navigating difficult personalities without surrendering your peace. Finding safety in an ordinary life: Why routines, healthy relationships, and the absence of drama can become some of the most meaningful signs of healing. One of the most moving moments comes when Orenda describes the ongoing grief of loving parents she can no longer safely have in her life. Noelani shares her own experience of estrangement and the realization that the safety she has created for her children is something she never experienced growing up. episodes.title: Abuse is Abuse, Narcissistic Abuse, Toxic Parents & Generational Trauma: A Therapist Explains....
episodes.description: Abuse is Abuse, Narcissistic Abuse, Toxic Parents & Generational Trauma: A Therapist Explains What We Get Wrong About Narcissism Do you need your parent to have a narcissistic personality disorder diagnosis to validate the abuse you experienced? Absolutely not. In this powerful episode of Beyond Mommy Dearest, I sit down with Luis, a California-licensed therapist currently living in Mexico City, for an honest, compassionate, and sometimes hilarious conversation about narcissistic abuse, personality disorders, generational trauma, and what it really means to heal. As two people with immigrant family backgrounds, we explore the intersection of culture, identity, family expectations, and childhood trauma. We talk about how our parents' experiences shaped them, how those experiences can influence the way they parent, and why understanding someone's history does not mean excusing their abuse. Luis brings his clinical expertise to a conversation that is often oversimplified on social media. Together, we unpack the difference between narcissistic traits and narcissistic personality disorder (NPD), why not every toxic person is a narcissist, and why survivors do not need a clinical diagnosis to recognize that what happened to them was wrong. I also share something deeply personal about my relationship with my oldest daughter, becoming a parent at a young age, and learning to acknowledge the ways I got things wrong. We discuss what separates imperfect parenting from harmful patterns of parenting: accountability, empathy, honesty, and the willingness to grow. Because our children don't need perfect parents. They need parents who are willing to repair, listen, and change. In this episode, we explore: Narcissistic personality disorder and the difference between narcissistic traits and a clinical diagnosis. How TikTok, social media, and pop psychology have changed the way we talk about mental health. The difference between a persistent lack of empathy and empathy fatigue. Why abuse does not require a diagnosis to be real or deserving of support. Gaslighting, manipulation, emotional abuse, and the internal chaos survivors can experience. The grief and anger that come with never receiving an apology from a narcissistic parent. Why going no contact with a parent is more complicated than a social media trend. Parenting, accountability, and repairing relationships with adult children. How immigrant family experiences, cultural expectations, and historical trauma influence generations. The survival behaviors children develop to please their parents and how those patterns can follow them into adulthood. Generational gifts, not just generational trauma, and choosing what we carry forward. The importance of human connection, community, and reconnecting with nature in an increasingly digital world. One of my favorite takeaways from this conversation: "It's really about the follow-through, the accountability, the honesty, and the growth." — Luis Healing isn't about spending the rest of your life trying to understand why your parent couldn't love you the way you needed. It's about recognizing what happened, honoring the child you once were, and deciding what you want your life to look like moving forward. And remember, you can understand your parents' trauma without accepting their abuse. You can appreciate your cultural heritage without continuing harmful family patterns. And you can break generational cycles without abandoning everything that came before you. About Our Guest Luis is a California-licensed therapist who currently resides in Mexico City and provides virtual therapy to clients in California. His professional background includes 10 years of working with parents before becoming a therapist. He brings a culturally responsive, intersectional perspective to conversations about mental health, relationships, identity, and healing. Luis also shares mental health education through social media. Although his practice has limited availability, he offers a waitlist and referrals for prospective clients. episodes.title: Breaking the Control: Nomz Bistline on FLDS, The False Prophet & Reclaiming Her Life
episodes.description: Reach out! You don't have to explain how crazy she was. We believe you!!! ⚠️ TRIGGER WARNING: This episode discusses religious trauma, coercive control, sexual and physical abuse, child exploitation, threats of violence and murder, incarceration, suicide attempts, suicidal thoughts, and death. What does it take to survive when fear, religion, manipulation, and coercive control have shaped nearly everything you believe? In this episode of Beyond Mommy Dearest, I sit down with Nomz Bistline, featured in The False Prophet, for a raw conversation about growing up in the FLDS, becoming entangled in Samuel Bateman's group, surviving extreme coercive control, spending 21 months in prison, and ultimately beginning to find herself again. Nomz takes us behind what viewers saw in the documentary and explains how years of religious conditioning made threats of punishment and damnation terrifyingly real. She shares how manipulation, fear, intermittent kindness, threats against people she loved, and relentless pressure eventually caused her to become numb and disconnect from her own intuition. We also talk about something far more complicated: how someone can be both accountable for their actions and a victim of profound coercive control. Nomz opens up about incarceration, surviving a suicide attempt, months of suicidal depression, and finally receiving therapy. Surprisingly, prison also gave her something she had rarely experienced before: the freedom to think and feel without being punished for it. During her darkest days, she began writing down ten things she was grateful for. Sometimes the glimmer was simply a bar of soap, clean clothes, a mattress, or a meal. Eventually, she became grateful for something much bigger: awareness. We talk about rebuilding self-trust, grieving family members who remain in the FLDS, learning what healthy love feels like, and why people on the outside often misunderstand survivors who stay, comply with, defend, or return to their abusers. Nomz describes survivors as clay models. Abuse, fear, manipulation, and conditioning can mold someone into what an abuser needs them to become. But underneath those layers is a foundation that was there all along. The real person is still there. And sometimes healing is the process of breaking away that clay, piece by piece, until you finally recognize yourself again. Because Nomz found those tiny glimmers and kept going, she is here. And now we all get to experience her glimmers, too. ❤️ If you or someone you know is experiencing suicidal thoughts or a mental health crisis in the United States, call or text 988 for immediate support. episodes.title: The False Prophet: How Cult Leaders and Narcissists Use the Same Psychological Abuse Tactics
episodes.description:
What happens when a narcissist gains absolute power?

In this powerful episode, I sit down with Dr. Christine Marie, featured in Netflix's Trust Me: The False Prophet, to discuss her undercover work helping expose Samuel Bateman and rescue women and children from coercive control.

While this story centers on a cult, the psychological tactics will sound incredibly familiar to anyone raised by a narcissistic parent or trapped in an emotionally abusive relationship.

We discuss:
• Why cult leaders and narcissists use the same manipulation tactics
• The psychology behind coercive control and brainwashing
• Why intelligent people can become victims
• The role of obedience, fear, shame, and isolation
• How confirmation bias and groupthink keep people trapped
• Why survivors often blame themselves
• What it really takes to "wake up" from psychological abuse
• How trust in yourself is rebuilt after manipulation
• The importance of community during healing
• Why leaving isn't about becoming stronger, it's about finally trusting yourself

If you've ever questioned your own reality because of narcissistic abuse, this episode will remind you that manipulation follows psychological principles, and your healing can too.

If this episode helped you, please subscribe, leave a review, and share it with someone who needs to hear that they are not alone.

More than most people realize.

Mark shares how his experience inside a manipulative organization led him to become obsessed with understanding narcissism and emotional control. What began as a search for answers eventually became the foundation for The Narcissist Playbook, where he interviewed self-confessed narcissists in an attempt to finally understand the mindset behind manipulation, gaslighting, shame, and coercive control.

Together, Noelani and Mark unpack the eerie parallels between cult leaders and narcissistic mothers, including:
* Love bombing and emotional conditioning
* Data mining and psychological manipulation
* Trauma bonding and control
* Gaslighting and self-doubt

* Idealism and exploitation
* Why survivors blame themselves

They also discuss the emotional aftermath of leaving manipulative systems, the grief that comes with realizing you were psychologically controlled, and how healing often requires rebuilding your relationship with yourself from the ground up.

episodes.description:
What happens when love, manipulation, control, and confusion all exist in the same relationship?

In this deeply validating episode of Beyond Mommy Dearest, Noelani sits down with counselor and criminologist Shalina Lodhia to unpack the hidden realities of narcissism, coercive control, intergenerational trauma, and emotional abuse. Together, they explore how subtle manipulation slowly erodes self-trust, why survivors often blame themselves, and how the body keeps score long after the abuse begins.

Shalina shares how her own lived experience witnessing domestic violence and coercive control in her South Asian community led her into counseling and advocacy work. The conversation dives into trauma bonds, gaslighting, narcissistic family systems, emotional invalidation, and the exhausting cognitive dissonance survivors experience when kindness and cruelty coexist in the same relationship.

This episode also explores:
* The connection between narcissism and coercive control
* Why survivors constantly question themselves
* The subtle signs of emotional abuse most people miss
* How trauma shows up physically in the body
* Why self-blame becomes a survival mechanism
* The difference between healthy conflict and manipulation
* The long-term effects of chronic emotional stress
* Why narcissists rarely seek therapy
* How to begin rebuilding self-trust after abuse
* The importance of journaling and external anchors
* Why healing starts with internal validation

We discuss cultural silence around abuse in Filipino, South Asian, and immigrant communities, and why these conversations are critical for breaking intergenerational cycles.
